messages:
alex: Heads-up: I'm testing a new key-minting flow for project-scoped API keys in staging. Goal is to reduce cross-project routing churn and make quota attribution more deterministic. rolling out canary tomorrow, want quick opinions.

michelle: what's the concrete diff vs the current service-key flow? is this just claims renaming or routing behavior changes too?

alex: Both. Main points: mint tokens per-project with a 'project' claim and optional 'delegate' claim. tokens issued from console include origin=console. Runtime routing will prefer exact project match -> org-fallback -> deny. Also we emit token_origin and route_taken telemetry.

jordan: how will quotas be charged? we can't double-count at org + project levels, or we'll overbill.

alex: quota plan: attribution is first-match: if token has project claim and route_used==exact_project then charge project quota. if falls back to org, charge org bucket. We'll add a telemetry tag "quota_target" to make it auditable.

samir: big concern: console can mint long-lived tokens. we should enforce TTL max and optional auto-rotation. also add a circuit-breaker for impersonation/impersonate claims.

kelly: console UX notes: need to show recommended TTL, a reason field for ops, and a visibility line "who can mint" + a small explainer about routing affinity and cost. also show estimated cost per 1k tokens. mock: add a small drawer that says "This key routes to project X (preferred). If project unavailable, will fall back to org Y."

alex: quick example of the mint API we're testing:

```
POST /v1/keys
{
  "project_id": "proj-123",
  "ttl_seconds": 86400,
  "claims": {"origin":"console","role":"read-only"}
}
```

infra-bot: deployer: key-service v0.9.1 -> staging (sha: abc123) :rocket:

ops-bot: sample telemetry emission: 
key_routing_match_total{route="exact_project"} 2345
key_routing_match_total{route="org_fallback"} 123
key_token_origin{origin="console"} 2450
failed_fallbacks_total 3

alex: Plan: enforce ttl<=30d for console-minted keys, emit token_origin + route_taken + quota_target, add console labels and copy, canary to 5% traffic tomorrow morning. @samir can you add quota-mapper logic? @kelly can you wire the UI copy + TTL guard? @jordan add dashboards for routing hit ratio / failed_fallbacks / token_origin.

michelle: sgtm :thumbsup: I'll run a couple of delegated-key edge cases (proxy key exchange, impersonation) once canary is live.

samir: on it. I'll open a PR for the quota mapper and add e2e tests to assert attribution. aiming EOD.

jordan: I'll add dashboard panels: routing_hit_ratio, token_origin_breakdown, failed_fallbacks, avg_latency_by_route. Alex — what's the exact log format you want?

alex: logs will include these fields: token_id, project_claim, route_taken, decision_reason, quota_target. I'll add them to the design doc: <https://go/key-minting-proposal>.

kelly: I'll prototype the UI drawer copy and TTL dropdown. will share mock by noon.

alex: thanks all — if you see anything weird in staging, tag me. canary starts 09:00 UTC.

michelle: noted, will smoke test auth flows right after deploy.

samir: PR opened: github.com/redwood/key-service/pull/456 (quota-mapper + tests).

jordan: dash panels created in observability staging space, shared links in the doc.

alex: closing loop — next steps: 1) TTL guard enforcement, 2) telemetry + dashboards, 3) console UI labels, 4) 5% canary -> 100% if healthy.

ops-bot: incident-bot: no alerts from canary window so far.

alex: perfect. follow-ups in the doc, thanks everyone.
